facts: Machu Picchu sits where the high Andes meet the Amazon Basin.
Machu Picchu was built in the fifteenth century, not in remote prehistory.
Stone terraces allowed agriculture on Machu Picchu's steep mountain slopes.
Machu Picchu's planned layout separated agricultural areas from residential ones.
The Machu Picchu sanctuary protects cloud forests as well as Inca ruins.
Machu Picchu's surrounding landscape includes a network of old roads and irrigation canals.
Machu Picchu's roughly 200 structures occupy a narrow ridge more than 2,400 metres above sea level.
Machu Picchu's exact astronomical role remains a subject of research.
The Machu Picchu sanctuary spans habitats from high grasslands down towards tropical forest.
Machu Picchu was abandoned during the sixteenth-century Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire.
The Mogao Caves preserve around a thousand years of Buddhist art.
A hidden library discovered at Mogao in 1900 contained tens of thousands of manuscripts.
Mogao's murals depict everyday life as well as religious scenes.
One Mogao mural shows a camel pulling a Silk Road trade cart.
A Mogao mural maps Mount Wutai with roads, rivers, temples and travellers.
The Mogao cave complex contains about 45,000 square metres of murals.
Mogao's art combines influences from India, China, Tibet and Central Asia.
Artists carved Mogao's sanctuaries into cliffs near the Dunhuang oasis.
Mogao's preserved caves extend over several levels of the cliff face.
More than 2,000 painted sculptures survive in the Mogao Caves.

source_title: UNESCO — Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor
facts: China's Terracotta Army includes horses as well as soldiers.
The Terracotta Army belongs to the burial complex of China's first emperor.
Bronze chariots were found in the first Qin emperor's enormous funerary complex.
The Terracotta Army preserves details of ancient uniforms and military equipment.
The soldiers' burial pits are only part of a much larger imperial tomb landscape.
The first Qin emperor's mausoleum was planned to echo his capital city.
Real weapons were buried with the Terracotta Army.
Qin Shi Huang standardised writing, weights and measures across his empire.
The Terracotta Army faces outward, symbolically guarding its emperor.
The Terracotta Army provides evidence of sophisticated pottery and metalworking in ancient China.
Mahabalipuram's five famous stone rathas were each carved from a huge boulder.
Mahabalipuram was a port city of the Pallava dynasty.
The word ratha means chariot; Mahabalipuram's stone temples resemble ceremonial chariots.
Mahabalipuram's monuments include both rock-cut caves and temples built from separate stones.
Mahabalipuram's giant outdoor relief is known as Arjuna's Penance or the Descent of the Ganges.
The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram stands directly beside the sea.
Excavation around Mahabalipuram's Shore Temple revealed structures buried beneath sand.
Mahabalipuram's carved shrines use the natural landscape as their building material.
The Olakkanesvara temple at Mahabalipuram stands on a rock near the lighthouse.
Mahabalipuram's rock carvings depict Hindu stories, royal figures and animals.
